test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 30 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements about an electric motor:

(a) An electric motor uses split rings.

(b) The direction of the force on the motor's coil can be found using Fleming's right-hand rule.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (a)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 3** is correct because an electric motor uses split rings for the commutator, which helps in reversing the direction of current in the coil every half rotation to ensure continuous rotation in the same direction.
 
• Statement (b) is incorrect because the direction of the force on the motor's coil is found using Fleming's left-hand rule, not the right-hand rule.
 
• Fleming's right-hand rule is used to find the direction of induced current in generators, not in motors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.
 
• The split ring commutator ensures that the direction of current through the coil is reversed every half turn, which keeps the coil rotating in the same direction.
 
• Fleming's left-hand rule states that if the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of the left hand are stretched mutually perpendicular to each other, with the forefinger in the direction of the magnetic field, the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of the force or motion of the conductor.
